walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Sampling — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Sampling brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Sampling.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: If a data set has an extreme outlier, which average is most affected?
options: 9xy, by adding all the numbers and merging the letters.
The mean — because every value (including the outlier) contributes to it.
The median is most affected because the outlier shifts the middle.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
7 - x — the minus sign outside the bracket changes the sign of every term inside (3 - x + 4).
3x - 12, by multiplying 3 by everything inside.
9xy, by adding all the numbers and merging the letters.
3 - x - 4 = -1 - x, by only applying the minus to the first term inside.
9xy, by adding all the numbers and merging the letters.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
8xy, by combining all terms regardless of variable.
5x + 3y — combine like terms (3x + 2x and 4y - y).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability mass function”?
options: PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Discrete vs continuous”?
options: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
